findings.title: Meningitis cases surge in Gaza as deteriorating living conditions put children at risk
findings.location: Nasser Medical Complex, Khan Younis, southern Gaza Strip
findings.affected_population_system: Pediatric emergency and inpatient capacity. Named pediatric specialist Dr Darwish Abu al-Khair reported 500–600 children attending the emergency department daily and said overcrowding prevents additional pediatric admissions, requiring transfers to other hospitals. The daily attendance figure is not a meningitis-specific case count. Neither the number of transfers nor their dates or destinations were verified.
findings.exact_supporting_passage: we no longer have the capacity to admit or accommodate additional children. As a result, we are transferring children to other hospitals
findings.source_type: News report by specialist outlet's Gaza correspondent; direct attributed interview with treating pediatric specialist

bounded_discovery_context.method: Targeted health search followed by full canonical article read, comparison with all 18 listed authenticated same-day prior heartbeats and detailed prior WAFA capacity finding.
bounded_discovery_context.novelty: Newly discovered explicit clinician-reported interhospital transfers because pediatric admissions are saturated, with quantified daily emergency attendance, distinct from prior WAFA individual capacity-related discharge and unspecified-period facility totals. Not a new outbreak or new incident this hour.
bounded_discovery_context.caveat: Exact publication hour and interview date unknown; cannot establish that first publication fell within the hour. Specific figures and transfers not independently verified; prior WAFA reporting supports general capacity pressure only. Article contains an unrelated apparent chronology error; no reliance on its military or ceasefire narrative. Do not count attendance as meningitis cases, sum with prior facility counts, or infer an official closure.
